questions.question: The length of the common chord of two circles of radii 18 cm and 16 cm is 19.2 cm. What is the distance between the centres of the two circles? [Give your answer correct to the nearest integer value.]
questions.solution:
Given:

The length of the common chord of two circles of radii 18 cm and 16 cm is 19.2 cm.

Concept used:

1. The line of centres of two intersecting circles perpendicularly bisects their common chord.

2. In a right-angled triangle, Height2 + Base2 = Hypotenuse2

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e93e5f34ef66feac0e6e3be94e2ed3585b1af931f4df700bc3f7c4936bac798b.png] 

Let, P and Q be the centres of the larger and smaller circles respectively.

So, PA = 18 cm, QA = 16 cm.

AB is the common chord. So, AB = 19.2 cm

According to the concept,

PQ perpendicularly bisects AB at D. So, AD = DB = 19.2/2 = 9.6 cm

Considering ΔADQ,

AD² + DQ² = QA²

⇒ DQ² = 16² - 9.6²

⇒ DQ² = 163.84

⇒ DQ = 12.8

Considering ΔADP,

AD2 + DP2 = PA2

⇒ DP2 = 182 - 9.62

⇒ DP2 = 231.84

⇒ DP ≈ 15.2

Hence, PQ = DQ + DP = 12.8 + 15.2 = 28

**∴ The distance between the centres of the two circles is 28 cm.**

questions.question: The length and the breadth of a rectangular cardboard are 40 cm and 35 cm, respectively. If the biggest possible square is cut out from this cardboard, what is the area of the remaining part of the cardboard?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To cut out the biggest possible square from a rectangle, its side must equal the smaller dimension (breadth).

Side of the square = 35 cm.

The remaining portion is a rectangle with length (40 − 35) = 5 cm and breadth 35 cm.

Remaining Area = 5 × 35 = 175 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 175 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of cardboard (L) = 40 cm

Breadth of cardboard (B) = 35 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth

Area of square = Side × Side

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3da016dd48823ff1757cf7324b566ebd4c7ef267854f3edd4cf1d3ff692582b7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the original cardboard = 40 × 35 = 1400 cm²

⇒ For the biggest possible square, Side (a) = Breadth = 35 cm

⇒ Area of the cut-out square = 35 × 35 = 1225 cm²

⇒ Area of the remaining part = Area of original cardboard − Area of cut-out square

⇒ Area of the remaining part = 1400 − 1225 = 175 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 175 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Maximum Square from a Rectangle

To cut the largest possible square from a rectangle, the side length of the square must be perfectly equal to the shorter side (breadth) of the given rectangle.

Area of a Rectangle

The area of a rectangle is defined as the product of its length and breadth. Formula: Area = L × B.

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total distance around the outside boundary of a rectangle. Formula: Perimeter = 2 × (L + B).

questions.question: ​If the HCF of two numbers (each greater than 17) be 17 and the LCM be 561, then find the sum of the numbers.
questions.solution:
Given:

HCF of two numbers (each greater than 17) be 17 and the LCM be 561.

Concept used:

1. Co-prime numbers are a set of numbers or integers which have only 1 as their common factor i.e. their highest common factor (HCF) will be 1.

2. LCM is the smallest common multiple of two or more numbers.

3. HCF of two or more numbers is the greatest factor that divides the numbers.

Calculation:

Let the number be 17a and 17b respectively. (where a and b are co-prime)

According to the concept,

LCM (17a, 17b) = 561

⇒ 17 × a × b = 561

⇒ ab = 33 ....(1)

The only possible pair that suffice the condition in (1) and both are co-prime, a = 11 and b = 3

Hence, the sum of the numbers

⇒ 17a + 17b

⇒ 17(a + b)

⇒ 17 × (11 + 3)

⇒ 238

**∴ The sum of the numbers is 238.**

questions.question: Shubham bought a book from Meesho at Rs. 500. Meesho also charged an additional Rs. 25 for packaging and Rs. 50 for delivering the book. For what amount should Shubham sell his book to make a profit of 16%?
questions.solution:
Given:

Shubham bought a book from Meesho at Rs. 500. Meesho also charged an additional Rs. 25 for packaging and Rs. 50 for delivering the book.

Profit% = 16%

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + Gain%)

Calculation:

Total cost price occurred to Shubham = 500 + 25 + 50 = Rs. 575

Now, the selling price = 575(1 + 16%) = Rs. 667

∴ Shubham should sell his book for Rs. 667 to make a profit of 16%.

questions.question: The cash difference between the selling prices of an article at a profit of 8% and at a loss of 4% is Rs. 54. Find the cost price of the article.
questions.solution:
Given:

The cash difference between the selling prices of an article at a profit of 8% and at a loss of 4% is Rs. 54.

Concept used:

1. Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + Gain%)

2. Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 - Loss%)

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the article be Q.

According to the concept,

Q(1 + 8%) - Q(1 - 4%) = 54

⇒ Q(1.08 - 0.96) = 54

⇒ Q = 54/0.12

⇒ Q = 450

∴ The cost price of the article Rs. 450.

questions.question: A certain number of identical spheres are formed by melting a large sphere of radius 28 cm. What is the number of small spheres formed if the surface area of each small sphere is 2464 cm²? [Use π = (22)/(7)]
questions.solution:
Given:

A certain number of identical spheres are formed by melting a large sphere of radius 28 cm.

The surface area of each small sphere is 2464 cm2.

Concept used:

1. Volume of a sphere = {4pi R³ over 3} (R is the radius of the sphere)

2. The curved surface of a sphere = 4πR² (R is the radius of the sphere)

3. Total volume of the small spheres must add up to the volume of the larger sphere.

Calculation:

Let the radius of each small sphere be r cm.

According to the concept,

4πr² = 2464

⇒ r² = 2464 ÷ 88/7

⇒ r² = 196

⇒ r = 14

Volume of each smaller sphere = (4/3 × π × 14³) cm³

Let's suppose, N number of small spheres can be made.

According to the concept,

N(4/3 × π × 143) = (4/3 × π × 283)

⇒ N × 14³ = 2³ × 14³

⇒ N = 8

**∴ The number of small spheres formed if the surface area of each small sphere is 2464 cm2 is 8.**

questions.question: In a city 60% of the population are males and the rest are females. If the ratio of married males to non-married males is 5 : 7, and the ratio of married females to non-married females is 2 : 3, then what percentage of the total population is married?
questions.solution:
Given:

In a city 60% of the population are males and the rest are females.

The ratio of married males to non-married males is 5 : 7 and the ratio of married females to non-married females is 2 : 3.

Calculation:

Let the total population be 600q.

Number of married male population = 600q × 60% × 5/(5 + 7) = 150q

Number of married female population = 600q × (100 - 60)% × 2/(2 + 3) = 96q

Now, the required percentage of the total population is married = frac {150q + 96q}{600q} times 100\% = 41%

**∴ 41% of the total population is married.**

questions.question: A1 alone can complete a piece of work in 14 days, A2 alone can complete the same work in 21 days, while A3 alone can complete the same work in 28 days. The three worked together, completed the work, and received a total payment of Rs. 1,040 for doing the work. What is A2’s share in the total payment received?
questions.solution:
Given:

A1 alone can complete a piece of work in 14 days, A2 alone can complete the same work in 21 days, and A3 alone can complete the same work in 28 days. 

The three worked together, completed the work, and received a total payment of Rs. 1,040 for doing the work.

Concept used:

1. Total work = Efficiency (Work done per day) × Total time taken

2. The wage amount is already distributed among the workers according to the ratio of their work done.

Calculation:

LCM (14, 21, 28) = 84

Let the total work be 84 units.

Efficiency of A₁ = 84/14 = 6 units

Efficiency of A₂ = 84/21 = 4 units

Efficiency of A₃ = 84/28 = 3 units

So, the ratio of work done by A₁, A₂ and A₃ = 6 : 4 : 3

Now, A2’s share in the total payment received = 4/(6 + 4 + 3) × 1040 = Rs. 320

**∴ A2’s share in the total payment received is Rs. 320.**

questions.question: Points A and B are 200 km apart. A person starts from A at 10 a.m. at a speed of 10 km/h and goes towards B. Another person starts from B at 11 a.m.at a speed of 20 km/h and goes towards A. At what time will they meet?
questions.solution:
Given:

Points A and B are 200 km apart. 

A person starts from A at 10 a.m. at a speed of 10 km/h and goes towards B. 

Another person starts from B at 11 a.m. at a speed of 20 km/h and goes towards A.

Concept used:

1. Distance = Speed × Time

2. Relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds while two objects come from opposite directions.

3. Time taken to meet for two objects coming towards each other = Intermediary distance ÷ Relative speed

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b52a3fdb28f5a2227f6c28db8dc766abc2b85e0a2c869a8e0722dfe68957040.png] 

When the second person started from point B at 11.00 a.m., the first person was at C.

Time between 11.00 a.m. and 10.00 a.m. = 1 hour

So, AC = 10 km (Since the speed of the first person is 10 km/h)

So, BC = 200 - 10 = 190 km/h

Hence, time taken by them two to meet at M = 190/(20 + 10) = 6frac {1}{3} hours

Now, they will meet at

⇒ 11.00 a.m. + 6frac {1}{3} hours

⇒ 05.00 p.m. + 1/3 hours

⇒ 05.00 p.m. + 1/3 × 60 minutes

⇒ 05.00 p.m. + 20 minutes

⇒ 05.20 p.m.

∴ They will meet at 05.20 p.m.

questions.question: A boat can travel in still water at 7 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. Find the total time (in hours) taken by the boat to travel 60 km upstream and return to the starting point.
questions.solution:
Given:

A boat can travel in still water at 7 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h.

Concept used:

1. While rowing upstream, the upstream speed is the difference between the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

2. While rowing downstream, the downstream speed is the addition of the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

3. Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

Upstream speed = 7 - 3 = 4 km/h

Downstream speed = 7 + 3 = 10 km/h

Now, the total time taken by the boat to travel 60 km upstream and return to the starting point

⇒ 60/4 + 60/10 = 21 hours

**∴ The total time taken by the boat to travel 60 km upstream and return to the starting point is 21 hours.**

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Length × Breadth = Area 

Length increased by 162over3 % = 1/6, means 7/6.

Since, the area of rectangle remains unchanged so the ratio is 1 : 1

And new ratio of length became old ratio of breadth, & old ratio of length became new ratio of breadth.

Now, % decrease in breadth = (7 - 6)/7 × 100 = **14.29%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

The length of a rectangle is increased by 16(2)/(3)% i.e. (50)/(3)%.

Concept used:

Area of a rectangle = Length × Breadth

Calculation:

Let the initial length of the rectangle be 90x and the breadth be y.

Area of the rectangle = 90xy

After (50)/(3)% increment, the length = 90x(1 + 50/3 %) = 105x

Since the area remains unchanged, the breadth becomes = 90xy/105x = 6y/7

Now, % decrease in breadth = frac {y - frac {6y}{7}}{y} × 100\% = 14.285% ≈ 14.29%

**∴ Its breadth should decrease by 14.29% so that the area of the rectangle remains unchanged.**
